title: tmux server livelock in tty_draw_line under control-mode load (separate from #4969)
body:
## Summary

tmux server enters a livelock (100% user-mode spin, never returns to `poll()`) inside the screen redraw path. All subsequent commands against the server (`tmux ls`, `tmux has-session`, `tmux info`, any new `attach-session`) queue on the command socket and never complete. Existing clients remain attached and visible but unresponsive. Recovery requires `SIGKILL` on the server PID — `tmux kill-server` and `SIGTERM` are both ignored (details in Workaround below).

## Related prior art

- **#4969** ("Bug: `tty_draw_line` enters long running loop under specific circumstances", closed 2026-04-04): same function, same loop, fixed by commit `cd60de44` which clamps `nx` at the top of `tty_draw_line`. **That fix is present in this build** (confirmed at lines 149–150 of `tty-draw.c@participant4`). This report is a different path into the same loop.
- **#4932** ("Infinite CPU loop in `screen_redraw_draw_scrollbar` due to unsigned integer underflow", open): different helper but same class — `screen_redraw_screen` → helper that can iterate billions of times.

## Environment

- macOS 26.4.1 (arm64, build 25E253)
- tmux build: **HEAD-dd62c2f** (reports as `next-3.7`), installed via Homebrew HEAD tap
  - `/opt/homebrew/bin/tmux -> ../Cellar/tmux/HEAD-dd62c2f/bin/tmux`
- Workload: ~5 concurrent control-mode clients (`tmux -C attach-session`) driven by `agent-deck` v1.7.50 (Go TUI that polls each tracked session every ~2s via `capture-pane`, `display-message`, `list-clients`, `set-option`). Sessions display Unicode-heavy content: braille spinners (`⠐⠁⠃⠇⠧⠷⠿`), box-drawing, emoji in `status-left`.

## Process state

Both incidents: process state in `ps`: `Rs` (runnable + session leader), not `S` or `D` — the event loop is *not* in a syscall. CPU consistent with a single-threaded spin at 100%. First incident server uptime at detection ~17h; second incident ~6h14m.

## Evidence: two independent incidents, five `lldb` samples

All samples: `lldb --batch -p <server_pid> -o "thread backtrace all" -o "detach" -o "quit"`, on the main thread (`com.apple.main-thread`), same binary (`HEAD-dd62c2f`), same machine, same workload.

- **Incident A** — ~17h server uptime, two samples ~60s apart
- **Incident B** — ~6h14m server uptime (server restart after A, same day), three samples 30s apart

All five samples share the **same outer call chain** with byte-identical return addresses:

```
tmux`tty_draw_line + 1000             ← present only when a helper is on the stack (A1, A2, B1, B2)
tmux`screen_redraw_screen + 2960
tmux`server_client_loop + 1856
tmux`server_loop + 100
tmux`proc_loop + 68
tmux`server_start + 568
tmux`client_main + 1040
tmux`main + 2032
```

What varies between samples is only the innermost on-CPU frame:

| Sample | Incident | Innermost PC | Frame above |
|--------|----------|--------------|-------------|
| A1 | A | `log_debug + 56` | `utf8_to_data + 204` → `tty_draw_line + 1000` |
| A2 | A | `utf8_to_data + 188` | `tty_draw_line + 1000` |
| B1 | B | `grid_get_cell + 24` | `tty_draw_line + 1000` |
| B2 | B | `utf8_to_data + 188` | `tty_draw_line + 1000` |
| B3 | B | `tty_draw_line + 1636` | `screen_redraw_screen + 2960` (no helper frame) |

Full stack of B3 (the most informative — CPU caught in `tty_draw_line`'s own loop body):

```
* thread #1, queue = 'com.apple.main-thread'
  * frame #0: tmux`tty_draw_line + 1636
    frame #1: tmux`screen_redraw_screen + 2960
    frame #2: tmux`server_client_loop + 1856
    frame #3: tmux`server_loop + 100
    frame #4: tmux`proc_loop + 68
    frame #5: tmux`server_start + 568
    frame #6: tmux`client_main + 1040
    frame #7: tmux`main + 2032
```

## Interpretation

The spin is localized to the inner cell-advance loop in `tty_draw_line` between offsets ~1000 and ~1636 — the loop body calls `grid_get_cell` to fetch the next cell and `utf8_to_data` to encode it for output. Samples A2 and B2 caught the CPU at the **exact same instruction** (`utf8_to_data + 188`) across incidents 6+ hours apart; sample B3 caught it inside the loop body with no helper on the stack. No sample has advanced past `screen_redraw_screen + 2960`.

Combined with on-CPU process state (not blocked on I/O), new `tmux` commands piling up indefinitely on the command socket, and the single-threaded model, this is a **redraw-path livelock**, not an I/O wedge.

## Root cause (source-level)

The `for (;;)` loop in `tty_draw_line` (`tty-draw.c@participant4`, line 230) advances its cell index `i` only here:

```c
/* Otherwise move to the next. */
current_state = next_state;
memcpy(&last, gcp, sizeof last);
if (empty != 0)
    i += empty;
else
    i += gcp->data.width;
```

The loop's only exit is `if (next_state == TTY_DRAW_LINE_DONE) break;` which requires `i == nx`. If a cell has `gcp->data.width == 0` and `empty == 0`, `i` does not advance and the loop spins forever, with the state machine cycling between (typically) `SAME` and `FLUSH` states as `buf` fills and drains — which is why samples A1 and A2 catch the CPU inside `log_debug` / `utf8_to_data + 188` (the per-cell debug log and output-encoding path are called every iteration).

`empty == 0` when the cell has non-default background *and* isn't classified as trailing empty by `tty_draw_line_get_empty`. `gcp->data.width == 0` is possible for a cell that contains only a zero-width character — e.g. a variation selector (U+FE0E / U+FE0F) or combining mark without its base character. An orphaned `GRID_FLAG_PADDING` cell (second half of a wide char whose first half was overwritten) would also reach this code path via line 268: `else if (gcp->flags & GRID_FLAG_PADDING) next_state = TTY_DRAW_LINE_PAD;` — PAD is not EMPTY or DONE, so `i += gcp->data.width` (which is 0 for a padding cell) is the result.

Note: the `nx` clamp added by #4969 (`if (atx + nx >= tty->sx) nx = tty->sx - atx;`) is present and working — the outer loop bounds are correct. The stuck condition is per-cell, not a runaway outer bound.

## Hypothesis for how the grid reaches this state

A control-mode client writing over an emoji-sequence cell or a wide character near a pane boundary can leave a grid cell where `data.width == 0` and `bg != default` (e.g. from `status-left` color attributes). Any subsequent `tty_draw_line` over that row livelocks at that cell. This is consistent with both incidents occurring only after hours of accumulated control-mode traffic.

## Reproduction conditions (observational, not a tight repro)

- Heavy control-mode poll traffic from `agent-deck` against ~5-7 persistent sessions
- Sessions display Claude Code UI (high-frequency spinner updates with braille glyphs, box-drawing, emoji in titles)
- Sessions driven via `claude --resume <uuid>`, so pane content includes long Unicode scrollback

Not yet tight-reproducible on demand. Observed twice on the same machine the same day: first at ~17h of steady load, then again ~6h14m after server restart.

## Workaround

`SIGKILL` (`kill -9`) on the server PID. `tmux kill-server` and `SIGTERM` were both ignored — consistent with a spin that never crosses a signal-check or command-queue boundary between render passes.

Full `lldb` output, `env.txt`, and sanitized agent-deck config available on request.

comments.body:
## Another reproduction: macOS arm64, CJK + truecolor rendering in Claude Code TUI pane

**Environment**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| tmux version | `next-3.7`, self-built from master commit [`4a926e4`](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/commit/4a926e489b8497ca1ed6f188aacfa0215b720371) (`2026-04-28 10:01 UTC`), ARM64 |
| OS | macOS 26.4.1 (Darwin 25.4.0 arm64, Apple Silicon Mac Mini) |
| libevent | 2.1.12-stable — **select** backend (not kqueue) |
| ncurses | 6.0 20150808 |
| Sessions / panes | 1 session, 71 panes at time of hang |
| Server uptime | ~14h52m (started 12:36, hung ~03:25 next day) |

**Symptoms — exact match with #5024**

- Server process pinned at **86–100% user-mode CPU** continuously (low RSS ~35 MB, not a memory issue)
- All new client connections froze: `tmux ls`, `tmux display-message` spawned processes at **100% CPU self-spinning**, never returned
- An already-attached client (`attach-session`) continued **receiving rendered output** from the server — confirming the server's write path to existing client fds was still running, but `poll()` was never re-entered
- **Three zombie child processes** (pane shells) accumulated for 5+ minutes without being reaped → `SIGCHLD` path not executing
- `SIGTERM` was ignored (sent manually, server did not exit). Only `SIGKILL` terminated the server

**Likely trigger**

The pane that was actively rendering at the time of hang was running **Claude Code** (a TUI application), which was streaming a response containing **Chinese/CJK text** with truecolor ESC sequences (`ESC[38;2;R;G;Bm`). The verbose server log (`-v`) shows a dense stream of `tty_draw_line` / `tty_clear_line` calls all targeting the same client fd (`/dev/ttys031`) with no inter-call gaps — consistent with the `for(;;)` loop in `tty_draw_line` never returning to the event loop.

**Log evidence (from `-v` server log, last ~8ms window before operator intervention)**

```
1777537422.876617 /dev/ttys031:  
1777537422.876631 /dev/ttys031: Review
...
1777537422.879153 /dev/ttys031: `update-acp-application-with-run-script.mdx`\357\274\214...  ← CJK UTF-8
...
1777537422.884106 /dev/ttys031: \033[106X    ← last entry, no further timestamps
```

All timestamps fall within an ~8ms window — the loop was clearly not returning between draw calls.

**Additional note: `select` backend**

This binary was built with libevent using the `select` backend rather than `kqueue` (visible in server startup log: `using libevent 2.1.12-stable select`). Not sure if this is expected for this build environment or relevant to the hang behavior — flagging it in case it affects event dispatch.

**Recovery**

`kill -KILL <server-pid>` terminated the server. Restarted cleanly with no config changes — server is now running normally at <1% CPU.

Happy to provide the trimmed `-v` server log or run a `sample` / `dtrace` trace on a future reproduction if that would help narrow down the exact loop entry point.

comments.body:
Second reproduction on the same Mac Mini, ~3 days after my 2026-04-30 note.

## Build / environment
- tmux: self-built master @ `4a926e48` (`next-3.7`)
  - `tty-draw.c:149-150` already contains the #4969 nx clamp
    (`if (atx + nx >= tty->sx) nx = tty->sx - atx;`), so this is confirmed
    to be the separate per-cell stall path #5024 tracks, not #4969.
- OS: macOS 26.4.1 (build 25E253), Darwin 25.4.0 arm64 (Apple Silicon Mac Mini)
- libevent: 2.1.12-stable (Homebrew, `select` backend in this build)
- ncurses: system 5.4 (`/usr/lib/libncurses.5.4.dylib`)
- Outer terminal: Ghostty, truecolor enabled in tmux
  (`set -as terminal-features ',*:RGB'`), `extended-keys on`, `allow-passthrough on`
- At time of hang: 5 sessions, 9 windows, **7 attached `attach-session` clients**
  (no control-mode / `tmux -C` clients)
- Statusline: gpakosz/.tmux framework + personal customisations; the status
  strings contain mixed-width glyphs (CJK paths in `#W`, ✳ U+2733, gpakosz
  powerline arrows) and run many `format_job` shell callbacks per redraw
  (`_username`, `_hostname`, etc.)
- Active TUIs in panes: `k9s`, Claude Code, neovim, lazygit
- Server uptime when CPU pegged: ~68h
- `status-interval 120` (so this is not driven by the periodic redraw timer)

## Symptom (matches #5024 exactly)
- Server pinned at 100% user-mode CPU, not in any syscall
- `tmux ls`, `tmux has-session`, `tmux attach` all hang indefinitely
- Already-attached clients still receive rendered output (write path keeps
  running; `poll()` is never re-entered)
- SIGTERM ignored; only SIGKILL terminates the server
- macOS `sample(1)` taken three times back-to-back: all 3894/3894 main-thread
  frames pinned in `server_client_loop → screen_redraw_screen → tty_draw_line`
  at the per-cell debug line.
- Killing the most active TUI (`k9s`) did **not** drop CPU — confirms the spin
  is internal to one `tty_draw_line` invocation, not driven by external pane
  activity.

## Workload differs from @reporter's
No control-mode, no `agent-deck`, no explicit per-2s `set-option -g status-left`.
On my side the mutation source is gpakosz's many `format_job` callbacks plus
normal pane activity. This supports the hypothesis from your patch session
that the orphan `GRID_FLAG_PADDING` path is reachable from any workload that
mutates a status-* string containing a width-2/width-1 glyph transition, not
just control-mode `set-option`.

## Caveat on the attached log
My build carries a small downstream patch in `log_debug` that drops messages
matching any substring from `TMUX_LOG_DROP`
(<https://github.com/participant2/tmux/commit/c95db4e3>). I had added `tty_draw_line:`
to that drop list earlier because the per-cell debug volume from `-v` (the
`if (log_get_level() != 0) log_debug(...)` at `tty-draw.c:281`) was large
enough to be **visibly user-affecting in interactive use** — typing lag in
panes during heavy redraws and ~1 GiB log growth per hour under normal
multi-pane work. Dropping that one prefix made `-v` usable for long-running
sessions while keeping every other category of debug output.

Consequence for you: the per-cell state-machine lines you read with
@reporter are **not** in the attached log. Only the downstream effects
(status redraw cascades, per-byte tty writes to attached clients) are visible.
The hang reproduces with or without `-v` — the patch only affects what reaches
disk, not whether the loop spins.

## Attached
Last 220 MB of the `-v` server log. Covers the storm window plus pre-storm idle baseline.

## Next reproduction
I'll rebuild with @reporter's `STALL` diagnostic patch and remove
`tty_draw_line:` from `TMUX_LOG_DROP` so the cell content actually lands in
the log. If/when it triggers again I'll post the three `STALL` lines (i, cell,
state) directly here.

[tmux-server-71140-last220M-2026-05-03.log.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27313615/tmux-server-71140-last220M-2026-05-03.log.zip)

### Third reproduction on this host — STALL detector `abort()` first to fire successfully

Following [my previous comment](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/5024#issuecomment-4365560112) where I rebuilt with @reporter's STALL detector patch but had only the bare livelock to report, the patched binary has now caught the issue in the act on this machine. The detector's `abort()` fired and the server self-terminated, producing both a tmux `-vv` trace of the stall site and a macOS crash report. Posting the artifacts here.

#### Stall site (last three lines of the `-v` log before `abort()`)

```
STALL i=103 px=0 py=16 nx=206 ex=206 atx=0 aty=17 wrapped=0
STALL cell: size=0 width=0 bytes=[] flags=0x4 attr=0x0 fg=8 bg=8 us=8 link=0
STALL state: current=PAD next=PAD empty=0 last.bg=8 defaults->bg=8 len=0 width=0 last_i=103
```

The signature matches @reporter's original capture exactly: `flags=0x4` (`GRID_FLAG_PADDING`) on a `width=0` cell, with both the current and next states classified as `PAD`. The orphan padding cell at column `i=103` blocks the `tty_draw_line` inner loop from advancing (`width==0 && empty==0` ⇒ `i` never increments).

#### Server / crash details

| | |
|---|---|
| binary | `next-3.7` master @ `9a94f486` + `4003b013` (reporter's STALL detector) |
| server pid | `84054` |
| `procLaunch` | `2026-05-03 02:23:53 -0500` |
| `procExitAbsTime` | `2026-05-03 10:35:48 -0500` |
| uptime to repro | **~8h 12min** |
| platform | macOS 26.4.1 (25E253), Apple Silicon (Mac16,10) |
| .ips bug_type | `309` (abort) |

For comparison, my previous repro on the same host took ~68 hours of uptime; this one tripped in ~8 hours, so the trigger frequency on this workload is higher than I previously estimated.

#### Workload (unchanged from prior comment)

- 7 attached clients (regular `tmux attach`, **not** control-mode — distinct from @reporter's setup)
- 5 sessions / 9 windows / 65+ panes
- Status line: gpakosz/.tmux + custom `format_job` callbacks; mix of CJK / `✳ U+2733` / powerline arrows (wide+narrow glyph mix)
- `status-interval=120`, so this is not a clock-driven hot path
- Active TUIs: k9s, Claude Code, nvim, lazygit

This further reinforces the hypothesis from the prior comment: **any workload that frequently mutates `status-*` strings containing wide↔narrow glyph transitions can trip this**, not just control-mode clients with high-frequency `set-option -g status-left` updates.

#### Attachments

- `tmux-server-84054.full.log.xz.zip` — full `-v` server log from launch (`02:23:53 -0500`) to the `abort()` (`10:35:48 -0500`), xz-compressed then zip-wrapped (GitHub doesn't accept `.xz` directly). 688 MB raw → 19 MB packaged. The STALL three lines are at the very end.
- `tmux-2026-05-03-103549.ips` — macOS crash report confirming the `abort()` path.

Happy to run further targeted patches if it would help narrow down the producer side (i.e., where the orphan PADDING cell is being written without its left half being cleared).

- [tmux-server-84054.full.log.xz.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27320851/tmux-server-84054.full.log.xz.zip)
- [tmux-2026-05-03-103549.ips.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27320854/tmux-2026-05-03-103549.ips.zip)

### 4th reproduction on this side — L2 (`screen_write_check_padding`) hit, *new* call path via copy-mode redraw

@participant1 With your `check_pad2.diff` plus the PAD `i++` fallback applied (on top of `master` + reporter's STALL detector), I just hit your `screen_write_check_padding` `assert(n > 0)` for the first time. Worth flagging because the call path is **different** from the three previous reproductions on my side, which all came through `tty_draw_line`.

**Crash facts**

- pid 41174, launched 2026-05-06 00:48:17 CDT, aborted 2026-05-06 02:07:29 CDT (~1h19m uptime)
- macOS 26.4.1 (ARM64), tmux next-3.7 master + participant1's two patches + reporter's STALL detector, ASAN **off**
- Signal: `SIGABRT` from `__assert_rtn` → `screen_write_check_padding` (screen-write.c:108)

**Stack (from macOS .ips, attached)**

```
screen_write_check_padding   screen-write.c:108     ← assert(n > 0) failed
screen_write_overwrite       screen-write.c:2401
screen_write_cell            screen-write.c:2133
window_copy_write_one        window-copy.c:4679
window_copy_write_line       window-copy.c:4874
window_copy_redraw_lines     window-copy.c:4960
window_copy_redraw_screen    window-copy.c:4974
window_copy_style_changed    window-copy.c:4984
server_client_loop           server-client.c:1471
```

So the orphan `GRID_FLAG_PADDING` cell was already sitting in a copy-mode pane's backing screen, and a `style_changed` notification from `server_client_loop` triggered `window_copy_redraw_screen` → eventually `screen_write_overwrite` → your check fired at the row tail. Previous three reproductions on my side all hit through `tty_draw_line` while drawing status / regular pane content; this one is the first that surfaces during a copy-mode redraw.

**What I'm missing this time**

I had switched the default server to run **without `-v`** (since the abort path makes log growth bounded, I had assumed I could rely on `.ips` alone). That means I do **not** have the `screen_write_check_padding: x=, y=` line nor the `screen_print` row dump for this hit — only the stack. Sorry about that.

**Next step on my side**

I've turned `-v` back on for the default server; the next L2 hit should give you the `screen_print` row dump you actually want. I'll reply with that as soon as I see it.

`.ips` attached for reference.

#### Build coordinates

- branch: `fix/log-drop-filter`
- HEAD: `2bf1c8f2f39321035b6d397b024cc108b6ee127d`

- ASAN: off. Platform: macOS 26.4.1 / arm64.

In this build, `screen_write_check_padding` lives at `screen-write.c:188-227`, with the `n==0` arm at lines 207-216 — replaced (vs. `next-3.7`) by a fork-and-lldb self-capture step before `abort()`. The original assertion semantics are unchanged.

#### How the core was captured (macOS 26 specific, brief)

macOS 26's AMFI suppresses user core writes for non-Apple binaries by default; the standard `kern.coredump=1` / `ulimit -c unlimited` recipe produces no file. The hook in commit `2bf1c8f2` forks a child that runs `lldb -p $$ --batch -o 'process save-core --style modified-memory ...'` and only then calls `abort()`. This produced a 21 MB Mach-O core. **The core is retained locally** — happy to query specific addresses / structs / fields and paste output on request, just not uploading the 21 MB binary itself.

#### Crash facts

- pid 58193, started 2026-05-06 11:08, aborted 2026-05-07 11:40:17 CDT (~24h32m uptime).
- `SIGABRT` from `__assert_rtn` → `screen_write_check_padding` (n==0 arm).
- Trigger: a copy-mode pane style change drove a 53-row full redraw.

#### Stack (consistent between `.ips` and lldb-on-core unwind)

```

server_client_loop ...
```

The 4th repro on my side also went through this same `window_copy_style_changed → window_copy_redraw_screen` path (no row dump and no core that time).

#### Frame locals at the abort

lldb caught the snapshot while the parent thread was sleeping in the hook's `sleep(1)` (inside `__semwait_signal`), so the `screen_write_check_padding` frame was still live:

```
screen *s     = 0xa74eb5400   (sx=147, sy=53, mode=17, cx=0, cy=2)
u_int   yy    = 2
grid   *gd    = 0xa74d10da0   (sx=147 sy=53 hsize=0 hlimit=0)

```

`s` is the copy-mode `window_copy_mode_data->screen` (the backing screen, not the tty backing).

#### Row 2 cell layout (i=140..165)

`grid_cell_entry` is 5 bytes packed. Flag bits seen here: `0x04`=GRID_FLAG_PADDING, `0x08`=GRID_FLAG_EXTENDED.

| i   | flags         | content |
|-----|---------------|---|
| 140 | 0x00          | inline space (fg=8 bg=8) |
| 141 | 0x00          | inline space |
| 142 | 0x08 EXT      | extddata[31] → ' ' width=1 size=1 |
| 143 | 0x00          | inline space |
| 144 | 0x08 EXT      | extddata[32] → ' ' width=1 size=1 |
| 145 | 0x00          | inline space |
| 146 | 0x08 EXT      | extddata[33] → ' ' width=1 size=1 |
| **147** | **0x04 PAD** | **inline data='!'** (the abort point) |
| 148 | 0x08 EXT      | extddata[34] → 0xE5 0x88 0x99 = `则` (U+5219) **width=2** |
| 149 | 0x04 PAD      | inline data='!' |
| 150 | 0x08 EXT      | extddata[35] → 0xE5 0xB7 0xAE = `差` (U+5DEE) **width=2** |
| 151 | 0x04 PAD      | inline data='!' |
| 152..163 | EXT/PAD alternating | 7 more width=2 CJK cells, each followed by a PAD |
| 164+ | 0x00         | back to plain spaces |

Full PADDING-cell scan over the row: i = 3, 33, 36, 38, 40, **147**, 149, 151, 153, 155, 157, 159, 161, 163, 173, 176, 178, 180, ...

When `screen_write_check_padding` reaches i=147: the cell at i=146 is width=1 (resetting n to 0), and i=147 is PAD with n=0 → abort.

The 9 width=2 CJK cells at i=148..163 are each immediately followed by a PAD at i=149/151/.../165 — that segment is internally consistent with width=2. The PAD at i=147 has no preceding wide cell to own it.

#### Plain observations (no causal claim)

- The screen affected is the copy-mode backing (scrollback buffer), not the tty backing.
- The trigger path `window_copy_style_changed → window_copy_redraw_screen` matches the 4th repro on my side.
- Across the full row of 294 cells, PAD cells appear in irregular places — some isolated (i=3), some in long stretches (i=147..163). The full list above is exhaustive for this row.
- `gl->flags = 2`, `hsize = 0`, `hscrolled = 0` (line is in the main grid area, not the history part).
- All PAD cells in this row carry inline `data = '!'` (0x21) with `fg=8, bg=8`. None of them are EXTENDED.

### 7th reproduction — same build as 6th; hits a **completely new entry path**: `input_parse → screen_write_collect_end`

**Build**: same as the 6th comment — HEAD `2bf1c8f2f39321035b6d397b024cc108b6ee127d` on `fix/log-drop-filter` at `https://github.com/participant2/tmux.git` (the lldb-attach core hook is in `2bf1c8f2`). Core is retained locally as before.

#### Crash facts

- pid 2978, aborted 2026-05-07 13:14:04 CDT (~1h34m after the previous abort, on the same restarted build).
- `SIGABRT` from `screen_write_check_padding` n==0 arm, with **i=0**.

#### Stack (entirely different from the 6th)

```
abort
tmux_save_core_via_lldb_then_abort
screen_write_check_padding(s=0x8e4816098, yy=71)   screen-write.c:212
screen_write_collect_end(ctx=0x8e481c510)           screen-write.c:2131
input_parse(ictx=0x8e481c500, len=88)               input.c:991
input_parse_buffer(wp=0x8e4815e00, len=88)          input.c:1048
input_parse_pane(wp=0x8e4815e00)                    input.c:1018
window_pane_read_callback                            window.c:1083
bufferevent_run_readcb_ ...
```

This is the 4th distinct entry on my side. The first six repros all went through redraw paths (`tty_draw_line` ×3, `window_copy_redraw_screen` ×3). This one goes through the **write path**: `screen_write_collect_end` calls `screen_write_check_padding(s, s->cy)` after each collect-flush, and on this flush it found the orphan PAD on the row the cursor sits on (yy=71, col 0).

#### Frame locals

```
screen *s     = 0x8e4816098      (sx=147 sy=79, mode=17, cx=7 cy=71)
u_int   yy    = 71
grid   *gd    = 0x8e4dcc780      (sx=147 sy=79, hsize=2739, hlimit=50000, hscrolled=2731)
grid_line *gl = 0x8e545cb18      (= &linedata[71]; see "Side note" below)
u_int   i     = 0                ← orphan at column 0; unambiguous
u_int   n     = 0
grid_cell gc  = { data="!" w=1 size=1, flags=0x04 GRID_FLAG_PADDING, fg=8 bg=8 }
```

`s` is a regular tty pane backing (not a copy-mode backing this time).

#### Row 71 cell contents (cellused=7, cellsize=36)

The actual visible row 71 (`linedata[hsize + yy] = linedata[2810]`), full content:

| i | flags | content |
|---|---|---|
| **0** | **0x04 PAD** | **inline data='!', fg=8 bg=8 — orphan, triggers the abort** |
| 1 | 0x40 CLEARED | inline space, fg=8 bg=8 |
| 2 | 0x40 CLEARED | inline space |
| 3 | 0x40 CLEARED | inline space |
| 4 | 0x40 CLEARED | inline space |
| 5 | 0x40 CLEARED | inline space |
| 6 | 0x08 EXT | extddata[0] → `'b'` (utf8_char=0x41000062, **width=1 size=1**), truecolor fg=#d77757 |
| 7..35 | — | uninitialized |

The entire row contains **no width>=2 cell at all** — just one width=1 letter `'b'` at col 6. The PADDING at col 0 cannot be explained as "the right half of a preceding wide cell". It is an absolute orphan.

#### Input buffer being parsed (88 bytes)

```
ESC[2D ESC[4B \r ESC[6C ESC[7A
ESC[38;2;215;119;87m b ESC[2C
ESC[38;2;235;159;127m t ESC[39m
\r \r\n \r\n \r\n \r\n \r\n \r\n \r\n
ESC[2C ESC[4A
```

Cursor moves and truecolor escapes only — **no UTF-8 multi-byte characters**. This buffer cannot make tmux emit a PAD by itself. So the PAD at col 0 was already on the row before this input arrived; `screen_write_collect_end` only spotted it post-hoc.

#### Side note: `screen_write_check_padding` indexes the line inconsistently

The diagnostic in this build (`screen-write.c:188-227`) currently is:

```c
struct grid_line *gl = grid_get_line(gd, yy);     // raw linedata[yy]
for (i = 0; i < gl->cellsize; i++) {
    grid_view_get_cell(gd, i, yy, &gc);            // view-coord; internally linedata[hsize+yy]
    ...
}
```

Callers pass `yy = s->cy` (a view-row). When `hsize > 0`, the two accesses pick **different lines**: the loop bound comes from `linedata[71]` (a history line, cellsize=73 here) while `grid_view_get_cell` reads from `linedata[2810]` (the visible row 71, cellsize=36).

This did not affect the present abort (i=0 is in range for both lines), but iterations past `cellsize=36` would behave according to whatever sits in `linedata[71]`, which can lead to false positives or misses on long history pages. Suggested fix:

```c
struct grid_line *gl = &gd->linedata[gd->hsize + yy];
```

or a small `grid_view_get_line` helper. This is a diagnostic-side fix, not a fix for #5024 itself.

- `tmux-precore-2978-bt.txt`
- `tmux-precore-2978-grid.txt`
- `tmux-server-2978.log` (filtered, ~654 KB)

```
1778379693.345885 tty_draw_line: cell 68341667 empty 1, bg 8; state: current EMPTY, next EMPTY
1778379693.345888 tty_draw_line: cell 68341668 empty 1, bg 8; state: current EMPTY, next EMPTY
...
1778379743.001063 tty_draw_line: cell 79644210 empty 1, bg 8; state: current EMPTY, next EMPTY
1778379743.001066 tty_draw_line: cell 79644211 empty 1, bg 8; state: current EMPTY, next EMPTY
```

`px + i` advances ~226k /sec. Across the 50 s window it grows from 68,341,667 to 79,644,211 (delta = 11,302,544 cells).

Two implications:

1. **`i` is advancing.** This is the difference from the four prior repros documented earlier in this thread — the `pad.diff.txt` "treat padding as empty" change (commit [`69487c2b`](https://github.com/participant2/tmux/commit/69487c2b)) is doing its job: `gcp->data.width == 0` is no longer trapping `i` in place.
2. **`i == nx` exit condition is unreachable.** Cell index has reached ~80 M, far beyond any plausible `tty->sx`. Strong suggestion that on this redraw path `nx` was computed as a very large unsigned (likely an `int` underflow into `~UINT_MAX` somewhere along `tty->sx - atx`, `nx - cx`, `ex - px`, or a caller-side computation), and the loop body keeps producing `empty=1` indefinitely.

Back-deriving from the rate (assume i started at 0 when the livelock entered): 79,644,211 / 226k cps ≈ 352 s ≈ 5.9 min, putting livelock onset around 21:23 - 5.9 min ≈ **21:16:30 CDT**.

### Normal vs. livelock prefix distribution

For comparison, here is the `log_debug` prefix tally on a 41-minute stretch of normal redraw activity captured into a sibling stderr mirror (`1.log`, 683.7 MiB real text, 20:24:07 → 21:05:36 CDT) versus the current 1 GiB livelock tail:

| | normal 41 min | livelock tail |
|---|---:|---:|
| `tty_draw_line:` | 5,827,835 | 100% (only prefix present) |
| `utf8_from_data:` | 1,459,219 | 0 |
| `utf8_to_data:` | 628,218 | 0 |
| `server_client_check_pane_buffer:` | 213,122 | 0 |
| `format_replace:` / `format_expand1:` | 351,147 | 0 |
| `cmdq_next` | 30,683 | 0 |
| 30+ other prefixes | various | 0 |

Once the loop enters this state, the server stops processing input parsing, format expansion, status, command queue — everything else. The redraw main loop monopolizes the server tick.

### Trigger

Unknown. I checked:

- shell history in the 21:14 – 21:24 window: empty (no user-issued commands)
- macOS unified log for `tmux` process in same window: only the regular ~1/min short-lived client-pid spawns from a status-line `_uptime` poll, no anomaly

So the trigger is whatever escape sequence one of the attached panes (claude / nvim / k9s / lazygit are typical here) emitted at ~21:16:30.

### Forensic gap — my side, not the patch

I do not have logs covering the actual transition from normal redraw into livelock. This is a **logging-side problem on my end**:

- Once the loop entered, verbose output blew up to **~27 MB/s** (per-cell `log_debug` emitted on every wedged iteration of the `for(;;)` loop in `tty_draw_line`).
- I had a sidecar log rotator wrapping the verbose stream (`MAX=2 GiB → KEEP=1 GiB`, poll every 10 s; trims by `tail -c 1 GiB` and rewriting in place).
- At 27 MB/s the rotator fired roughly every 37 s during the livelock. By the time I attached and SIGKILL'd at 21:29, the rotator had run something on the order of 20+ trim cycles, each one discarding the oldest 1 GiB of the on-disk log. The bytes covering the *exact* nx-bloat moment at 21:16:30 were among the first to be discarded.
- The 1 GiB I do have starts at 21:21:33 — already 5 minutes into the livelock — so it shows the steady-state pathology but not the entry.

For the next reproduction I'm tightening the rotator (smaller poll window, larger keep window, and a separate ring just for the first 30 s after a write-rate anomaly trips), and adding a cheap source-level guard at the loop entry to abort the moment `nx` is implausible — so the next occurrence captures the caller frame and the offending `nx` / `atx` / `px` / `tty->sx` directly via macOS `.ips`:

```c
/* tty-draw.c, near line 232 (start of the for(;;) loop) */
if (nx > 100000) {
    log_debug("%s: SUSPICIOUS nx=%u px=%u py=%u atx=%u sx=%u",
              __func__, nx, px, py, atx, tty->sx);
    abort();
}
```

Decision update on the build config: I'll keep ASAN **enabled** for the next run rather than disable it as I'd originally planned. The earlier-morning crash (`tmux-2026-05-09-020258.ips`, attached) is a #4962 heap-use-after-free in `grid_free_line` ← `grid_clear_lines` that ASAN caught cleanly via `___BUG_IN_CLIENT_OF_LIBMALLOC` — without ASAN that path would have been silent corruption. With the new `nx > 100000` abort guard preventing the livelock from spiralling, ASAN's per-call overhead no longer dominates a multi-minute runaway log; it just costs a constant factor on the healthy path, which is worth the diagnostic coverage on the still-open #4962 path that lives on the same branch.

- `tmux-2026-05-09-020258.ips` — separate `.ips` from a #4962 abort earlier the same day (`grid_free_line` ← `grid_clear_lines` ← invalid free), included for completeness but not the same incident
